Fact.Name: Kansas standard deduction, single
Fact.Description: Form K-40 line 4 for a single filer. K.S.A. 79-32,119(c)(2): "For tax year 2024, and all tax years thereafter, the standard deduction amount of an individual, including husband and wife who are either both residents or who file a joint return as if both were residents, shall be as follows: Single individual filing status, $3,605; married filing status, $8,240; and head of household filing status, $6,180." 2025 Kansas Individual Income Tax Booklet (ip25, rev. 9-26-25), page 6, Kansas Standard Deduction: "Single $3,605." Head of household and married filing separate are not in scope. These are the 2025 booklet amounts. Re-pin this amount from the 2026 booklet when it is posted.

Fact.Name: Kansas standard deduction, married filing jointly
Fact.Description: Form K-40 line 4 for a joint return. K.S.A. 79-32,119(c)(2): "married filing status, $8,240." 2025 Kansas Individual Income Tax Booklet, page 2: "Married Filing Joint $8,240." Married filing separate is not in scope. These are the 2025 booklet amounts. Re-pin this amount from the 2026 booklet when it is posted.

Fact.Name: Kansas exemption allowance, single
Fact.Description: Form K-40 line 5 for a single filer. K.S.A. 79-32,121(a)(2): "in the case of all other individuals with a filing status of single, head of household or married filing separate, a personal exemption of $9,160." 2025 Kansas Individual Income Tax Booklet, page 6: "If your filing status is single, married filing separate or head of household, check the box to indicate filing status, enter one in the box for number of exemptions and $9,160 in the amount box." No dependents are in scope, so the $2,320 dependent exemption is not added. These are the 2025 booklet amounts. Re-pin this amount from the 2026 booklet when it is posted.

Fact.Name: Kansas exemption allowance, married filing jointly
Fact.Description: Form K-40 line 5 for a joint return. K.S.A. 79-32,121(a)(1): "In the case of married individuals filing a joint return, a personal exemption of $18,320." 2025 Kansas Individual Income Tax Booklet, page 6: "If your filing status is married filing joint, check the box to indicate filing status, enter 2 in the box for the number of exemptions and $18,320 in the amount box." These are the 2025 booklet amounts. Re-pin this amount from the 2026 booklet when it is posted.

Fact.Name: Kansas income tax rate above the second bracket
Fact.Description: Tax Computation Worksheet column (b) when line 7 is over $100,000. K.S.A. 79-32,110b(a)(2)(B), for tax year 2024 and all tax years thereafter: "Over $23,000 $1,196 plus 5.58% of excess over $23,000." Subsection (a)(1)(B) uses the same 5.58% rate for a joint return over $46,000. 2025 booklet, page 34, Tax Computation Worksheet: "5.58% (.0558)." Stored as 558/10000. The amount on line 8 is rounded once, half up, to the dollar.

Fact.Name: Kansas tax worksheet subtraction, single
Fact.Description: Tax Computation Worksheet column (d) for a single filer when line 7 is over $23,000. 2025 booklet, page 34: "5.58% (.0558)" and subtraction amount "$87." K.S.A. 79-32,110b(a)(2)(B) states "$1,196 plus 5.58% of excess over $23,000." Five and fifty-eight hundredths percent of $23,000 is $1,283.40, and $1,283.40 minus $1,196 is $87.40. The worksheet subtracts $87, which is $0.40 less. The form uses the worksheet. Re-pin this amount from the 2026 booklet when it is posted.

Fact.Name: Kansas tax worksheet subtraction, married filing jointly
Fact.Description: Tax Computation Worksheet column (d) for a joint return when line 7 is over $46,000. 2025 booklet, page 34: "5.58% (.0558)" and subtraction amount "$175." K.S.A. 79-32,110b(a)(1)(B) states "$2,392 plus 5.58% of excess over $46,000." Five and fifty-eight hundredths percent of $46,000 is $2,566.80, and $2,566.80 minus $2,392 is $174.80. The worksheet subtracts $175, which is $0.20 more. The form uses the worksheet. Re-pin this amount from the 2026 booklet when it is posted.

Fact.Name: Kansas tax table limit
Fact.Description: Form K-40 line 8 uses the tax tables when line 7 is this amount or less. 2025 booklet, page 7: "If line 7 is $100,000 or less, use the Tax Tables beginning on page 27 to find the amount of your tax. If line 7 is more than $100,000, you will need to use the Tax Computation Worksheet on page 34 to compute your tax." Page 34 of the table: "100,001 and over – use the Tax Computation Worksheet." The 2025 table is not modeled. Line 7 of $100,000 or less stops. Re-pin this amount from the 2026 booklet when it is posted.

Fact.Name: Kansas residency answers
Fact.Description: Full-year resident is the supported Form K-40. Part-year residents and nonresidents complete Schedule S Part B. A joint return is a full-year Form K-40 only when both spouses lived in Kansas all year.

Fact.Name: Kansas residency
Fact.Description: Full year means you, and your spouse if you file jointly, lived in Kansas all year. Part-year and nonresident stop. Form K-40 and Schedule S Part B.

Fact.Name: Kansas residency is part-year or nonresident
Fact.Description: True for Schedule S Part B. Incomplete until /ksResidencyStatus is answered.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 1 federal adjusted gross income
Fact.Description: Federal AGI. 2025 Form K-40, line 1: "Federal adjusted gross income (as reported on your federal income tax return)."

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 2 modifications
Fact.Description: Zero. Schedule S modifications are not in scope. 2025 Form K-40, line 2: "Modifications (from Schedule S, line A27)."

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 3 Kansas adjusted gross income
Fact.Description: Line 2 added to or subtracted from line 1. Line 2 is zero, so this equals line 1. 2025 Form K-40, line 3.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 4 standard deduction
Fact.Description: $3,605 for single. $8,240 for married filing jointly. Other filing statuses use the single amount and stop. K.S.A. 79-32,119(c)(2). Itemized deductions stop the return, so this is the standard deduction. Age 65 and blindness stop, so the page 6 worksheet for people 65 or older or blind is not used.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 5 exemption allowance
Fact.Description: $9,160 for single. $18,320 for married filing jointly. K.S.A. 79-32,121(a). Dependents, a child born this year, a stillbirth, and the disabled-veteran exemption are not in scope. Being claimed as a dependent stops the return.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 6 total deductions
Fact.Description: Add lines 4 and 5. 2025 Form K-40, line 6.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 7 taxable income
Fact.Description: Subtract line 6 from line 3. If less than zero, enter 0. 2025 Form K-40, line 7, and 2025 booklet, page 7, LINE 7.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 7 is over the tax table
Fact.Description: True when line 7 is more than $100,000, so line 8 uses the Tax Computation Worksheet. $100,000 or less uses the tax tables, which are not modeled, and stops.

Fact.Name: Kansas tax worksheet subtraction
Fact.Description: $87 for single. $175 for married filing jointly. Other filing statuses use $87 and stop. 2025 booklet, page 34, Tax Computation Worksheet, column (d).

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 8 after the cent-then-dollar round
Fact.Description: Round(line 7 times 5.58% minus the worksheet subtraction). Dollar times Rational scales to cents half-even before Round half-up, so a product whose exact fraction is just under half a dollar can become 50 cents and then round up a dollar. 100,224 times 0.0558 is 5,592.4992. Minus $87 is 5,505.4992, which that path turns into 5,506. This is not the amount entered on the form.

Fact.Name: One hundred times the exact Form K-40 line 8
Fact.Description: Line 7 times 558/100, minus 100 times the worksheet subtraction. That is 100 times (line 7 times 0.0558 minus the subtraction), and for a whole-dollar line 7 it keeps the exact hundredth of a cent. 100,224 times 558/100 is 559,249.92, which is 5,592.4992 dollars. Minus $8,700 is 550,549.92 cents, which is 5,505.4992 dollars. The 5.58% rate itself is /ksTaxRate.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 8 tax
Fact.Description: Line 7 times 5.58 percent, minus $87 or $175, rounded once, half up, to the dollar. Computed only when line 7 is more than $100,000. Otherwise this fact is incomplete and the return stops, because the tax tables are not modeled. The cent-then-dollar result is one dollar high when it exceeds this exact product by more than 50 cents. 100,224 times 0.0558 minus $87 is 5,505.4992 and stays 5,505. 2025 booklet, page 34: "Subtract (d) from (c). Enter total here and line 8 of K-40." The form says whole dollars only. K.S.A. 79-32,110b(a).

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 12 total income tax
Fact.Description: Residents add lines 8 and 11. Line 11 is zero because there is no lump-sum distribution, so this equals line 8. Lines 9 and 10 are skipped for a resident. 2025 booklet, page 7, LINE 12.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 16 subtotal
Fact.Description: Subtract lines 13, 14, and 15 from line 12. Those credits are zero in scope, so this equals line 12. A federal Form 2441 credit greater than zero stops, so the 50 percent Kansas credit on line 14 is not calculated. 2025 Form K-40, line 16.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 18 total tax balance
Fact.Description: Subtract line 17 from line 16, not below zero. Line 17 is zero because the federal earned income credit is zero in scope, so this equals line 16. A federal earned income credit greater than zero stops, so the 17 percent Kansas credit is not calculated. 2025 booklet, page 8, LINE 18.

Fact.Name: This W-2's Kansas withholding
Fact.Description: Box 17 when box 15 is Kansas (the same state as the residence). A blank box 15 is in scope and contributes zero. A box 15 for another state stops the return and contributes zero here.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 19 Kansas income tax withheld
Fact.Description: Sum of W-2 box 17 where box 15 is Kansas. 2025 booklet, page 8, LINE 19: "Add the Kansas withholding amounts shown on your W-2 forms."

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 27 total refundable credits
Fact.Description: Add lines 19 through 25 and subtract line 26. Lines 20 through 26 are zero, so this equals line 19. 2025 Form K-40, line 27.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 28 underpayment
Fact.Description: If line 18 is greater than line 27, the difference. Otherwise zero. 2025 Form K-40, line 28.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 32 amount owed
Fact.Description: Add lines 28 through 31 and lines 35 through 42. Interest, penalties, and the contribution lines are zero, so this equals line 28. 2025 Form K-40, line 32.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 33 overpayment
Fact.Description: If line 18 is less than line 27, the difference. Otherwise zero. 2025 Form K-40, line 33.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 line 43 refund
Fact.Description: Subtract lines 34 through 42 from line 33. The credit-forward and contribution lines are zero, so this equals line 33. 2025 Form K-40, line 43.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 zero
Fact.Description: Printed on lines this return does not calculate: modifications, credits, estimates, penalties, and contributions. Those cases stop or are not offered.

Fact.Name: Form K-40 exemption count
Fact.Description: 1 for single. 2 for a joint return. 2025 booklet, page 6. Dependents are not in scope.

Fact.Name: Federal income other than W-2 wages
Fact.Description: Interest, tax-exempt interest, Social Security, a sale or capital gain, 1099-MISC, a 1099-R, Schedule C, or Schedule E. Any of that income stops a Form K-40.

Fact.Name: Dependents or a qualifying person
Fact.Description: Anyone in the household, or a filer who is a qualifying person for the child and dependent care credit. The $2,320 dependent exemption and the line 14 credit are not calculated.

Fact.Name: Age 65 or blind
Fact.Description: Primary filer is 65 or older or blind. On a joint return, either spouse. 2025 booklet, page 6: "If you or your spouse is over 65 and/or blind, complete WORKSHEET for Standard Deduction for People 65 or Older and/or Blind." That worksheet is not calculated. The spouse is checked only on a joint return so a single return does not wait on the spouse.

Fact.Name: Filer can be claimed as a dependent
Fact.Description: The primary filer, or either spouse on a joint return. 2025 booklet, page 6: "If you are claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer, enter 0 in the number of dependents box." The dependent standard deduction is not applied. The spouse is checked only on a joint return.

Fact.Name: Filing status other than single or joint
Fact.Description: The supported Form K-40 is single, or married filing jointly with both spouses in Kansas all year. Head of household, married filing separately, and qualifying surviving spouse are not calculated. A federal qualifying surviving spouse would check the Kansas head of household box. 2025 booklet, page 6, FILING STATUS.

Fact.Name: Federal Schedule 1-A is more than zero
Fact.Description: Qualified tips, overtime, car-loan interest, or the senior deduction on Schedule 1-A line 44. The READY spec calls this stop 1040 line 13b. The 2026 draft Form 1040 in this tool prints Schedule 1-A on line 13a and the qualified business income deduction on line 13b. Kansas conformity for Schedule 1-A is not pinned, so the deduction is not entered. Incomplete when line 44 is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Federal earned income credit is more than zero
Fact.Description: Form K-40 line 17 is 17 percent of the federal earned income credit. 2025 booklet, page 8, Earned Income Tax Credit Worksheet: "Kansas EITC (multiply line 1 by 17%)." That credit is not calculated. Incomplete when the federal credit is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Federal Form 2441 credit is more than zero
Fact.Description: Form K-40 line 14 is 50 percent of the federal child and dependent care credit. 2025 booklet, page 8, LINE 14: "Multiply amount of credit allowed on (federal Form 2441) by 50%." That credit is not calculated. The federal amount is Form 2441 line 11. Incomplete when that credit is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: Kansas part-year or nonresident
Fact.Description: Schedule S Part B is not calculated. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return. Incomplete until /ksResidencyStatus is answered.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: a W-2 box 15 is not Kansas
Fact.Description: Any W-2 whose box 15 is a state other than Kansas. A blank box 15 is in scope and is not this stop. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: income other than W-2 wages
Fact.Description: Any federal income other than W-2 wages. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: dependents
Fact.Description: The dependent exemption and the line 14 credit are not calculated. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: age 65 or blind
Fact.Description: The page 6 standard-deduction worksheet is not calculated. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: claimed as a dependent
Fact.Description: The dependent standard deduction is not calculated. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: filing status other than single or joint
Fact.Description: Head of household, married filing separately, and qualifying surviving spouse are outside this Form K-40. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: itemized deductions
Fact.Description: Kansas Schedule A is not calculated. 2025 booklet, page 7: "To compute your Kansas itemized deductions you must complete Kansas Schedule A." Complete false when this is not a Kansas return. Incomplete until the itemizing choice is answered.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: federal earned income credit
Fact.Description: Line 17, 17 percent of the federal earned income credit, is not calculated. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: federal Form 2441 credit
Fact.Description: Line 14, 50 percent of the federal child and dependent care credit, is not calculated. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: federal Schedule 1-A deduction
Fact.Description: Schedule 1-A line 44 is greater than zero, including qualified overtime. The READY spec names that stop as 1040 line 13b. This draft prints Schedule 1-A on line 13a. Kansas conformity is not pinned. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return and when line 44 is zero.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: line 7 is in the Kansas tax table
Fact.Description: Line 7 is $100,000 or less. The 2025 tax table is not modeled. Complete false when this is not a Kansas return. Incomplete until line 7 is complete.
